title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر -الشريط الرابع
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape four
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وصلى الله وسلم على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله و أصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته.

أما بعد فيقول الحافظ رحمه الله: " الخبر إما أن يكون له طرق بلا عدد معين أو مع حصر بما فوق الاثنين أو بهما أو بواحد" بدأ رحمه الله هنا تقسيم الحديث باعتبار عدد الناقلين، وقد سبق أن هذا التقسيم ينقسم به الحديث تقسيمين التقسيم الأول باعتبار عدد الناقلين في كل طبقة، والتقسيم الثاني باعتبار عدد الطبقات، فبدأ بتقسيم الحديث باعتبار عدد الناقلين في كل طبقة فقال إما أن يكون له طرق والمقصود بالطرق الأسانيد وهي جمع طريق والطريق في الأصل السبيل المسلوك والمقصود به في الاصطلاح الناقلون للحديث الذين رووه حتى وصلوه إلى منتهاه، ومنتهاه إن كان مرفوعا هو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن كان موقوفا هو الصحابي وإن كان مقطوعا هو التابعي ومن دونه..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. May God bless our master Muhammad and grant him peace, and his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: al-Hafiz, may God have mercy on him, says: "The report either has routes without a determinate number, or with a limit above two, or with those two, or with one." Here he began, may God have mercy on him, the division of the hadith by the number of transmitters. It has already been said that the hadith is divided by this into two divisions: the first by the number of transmitters in each layer, and the second by the number of layers. So he began with the division of the hadith by the number of transmitters in each layer, and said "either it has routes". What is meant by routes is the chains of transmission; it is the plural of ṭarīq, and ṭarīq is originally the road that is travelled, and what is meant by it as a technical term is the transmitters of the hadith who narrated it until they brought it to its end-point. Its end-point, if the report is traced to the Prophet (marfūʿ), is the Prophet, upon whom be God's blessing and peace; if it stops at a Companion (mawqūf), it is the Companion; and if it stops at a Successor (maqṭūʿ), it is the Successor and those below him..

flags.context: the third of the three end-points of a chain of transmission
options: a report stopping at a Successor (maqṭūʿ)
flags.note: Not in the project glossary, which fixes marfūʿ and mawqūf but not maqṭūʿ. The rendering has been built to match those two. It is important that maqṭūʿ ('stopping at a Successor', a classification by end-point) not be confused with munqaṭiʿ ('interrupted', a defect in the chain), which option 1 invites. The glossary should be extended with maqṭūʿ and munqaṭiʿ together.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

This record belongs to the Sheikh's commentary on Ibn Hajar al-ʿAsqalani's Nukhbat al-Fikr, a short manual of hadith terminology. The CMS holds the tapes out of order across ids 628–637 and the tape numbers in the titles do not run with the ids; the series should be ordered by the tape number in the title, not by id, and even then a gap remains (see the note on the download filenames).

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text is the opening of a lecture and breaks off; the full transcript is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
'Al-Hafiz' is Ibn Hajar al-ʿAsqalani, the author of the Nukhbah; the Sheikh refers to him by the title throughout rather than by name.

'Layer' renders ṭabaqah, a generation or level of the chain. The two divisions the Sheikh distinguishes — by the number of transmitters within each layer, and by the number of layers — are the framework for everything that follows, and the distinction has been kept sharp in the English.
The quoted matn is a compressed enumeration in the Arabic and reads awkwardly in English by design; it is Ibn Hajar's text, not the Sheikh's prose, and has not been smoothed.
'With those two' renders bihimā, i.e. limited to exactly two transmitters.
